newsitem.title: USA: W. Va. gov-elect eyes budget stabilization.
newsitem.headline: W. Va. gov-elect eyes budget stabilization.

text.p: West Virginia Gov.-elect Cecil Underwood said he hoped to keep the state's budget at $2.5 billion without creating new taxes.
"I hope we can stabilize it at that level," Underwood said in an interview broadcast Wednesday on C-SPAN.
The Republican governor-elect said his administration would emphasize using technology to create jobs, improve education and maintain the environment.
He said he would also work to keep down the cost of government. Underwood was elected governor in 1956, when the state budget was $15 million a year and the state population was slightly larger.
"That gives you some idea how the government has grown in this state," he said.
Underwood defeated former state Sen. Charlotte Pritt, the Democrat nominee, Nov 5.
